text.p: These are the main stories in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Under the income tax law, Lithuanians who were paid salaries abroad must also pay 20 percent income taxes at home. The new double taxation hits hardest well-known sportsmen, artistist and scientists.

- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told President Algirdas Brazauskas that on May 1 the budget collected 40 million litas of revenues more than planned. It is the first time since 1992 that the state budget was in surplus.
- Brazauskas will move to a new residence in central Vilnius in the middle of May.
- Four Western banks are ready to issue a $200 million credit for the construction of Butinge oil terminal but they request a state guarantee.
- International fair AgroBalt'97 opens its doors in Vilnius today. It attracted a record number of participants, 458 companies from 21 country.
- Magazine Euromoney forecast 3.74 percent GDP growth in Lithuania this year and 4.04 percent growth in 1998.
- Chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis urged the head of the state archives to resign archive documents of the interior ministry were destroyed last week.
- Influential U.S. defence expert group Jane's said that according to all official criteria the Baltic countries could become the first new members of NATO but this is strongly opposed by Russia.
- Vagnorius promised to raise salaries for doctors and teachers from July 1.
- Landsbergis is expected to announce his intention to be a candidate to the post of president on Saturday, newspaper sources said.
- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas continues his three day visit to Italy.
